nodes.label: graphify maintenance discipline
nodes.rationale: Commit GRAPH_REPORT.md and graph.json but never graphify-out/cache/; v5 tracked ~180 cache files by accident.

nodes.label: doctor exit code contract
nodes.rationale: 0 all pass, 1 at least one FAIL, 2 warnings only; CI and make demo both refuse to proceed on 1.

nodes.label: doctor.py check contract
nodes.rationale: The single highest-leverage file for the clone experience: it answers 'why can't I run this?' before the user has to read a stack trace. Every FAIL carries a runnable command or a document anchor, and credentials are reported set/unset/expired with no value ever printed.

nodes.label: Local compose stack design
nodes.rationale: The API runs on the host rather than in compose so the edit-reload loop stays fast during Phases 3-8; a cloner never runs a second command to see the dashboard.

nodes.label: Standing exit criterion (spec)
nodes.rationale: What prevents the retrofit; the local stack is exercised continuously rather than rotting.

nodes.label: The three-tier contract
nodes.rationale: Higher tiers are additive, never prerequisites; tier 0 is the promise and must work offline on a clean clone with no .env edits.

nodes.label: Secret handling rules
nodes.rationale: Never log a token, not even truncated; the refresh-token secret keeps a short version retention policy because old versions are expired credentials.

nodes.label: No-secrets-in-output guarantee (spike)
nodes.rationale: Proven by test, not by inspection: the report must not contain the token, not even a truncated prefix. The token file is also opened 0600 rather than chmod'd afterwards, because write-then-chmod leaves a window in which it is world-readable.

nodes.label: Injected-probe check design
nodes.rationale: Every check is a pure function returning a CheckResult with its environment probe injected as a parameter, so the whole suite runs with no Docker, no network, and no gcloud.

nodes.label: Leak-canary secret test
nodes.rationale: An earlier draft asserted the substring SECRET never appears, which false-positives immediately because the variable is named GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET and printing the name is the point; the invariant is that the value never appears, so values carry a canary that cannot collide with any variable name.

nodes.label: make doctor — tier-aware preflight

nodes.label: sync-down session end (~3 min)
nodes.rationale: Backs up, verifies the backup, then destroys. It will not destroy anything until it has confirmed both backups exist — a failed export leaves the tier up and tells you so rather than silently discarding a month of work. Between sessions the billable tier costs $0.

nodes.label: sync-up session start (~11 min)
nodes.rationale: Creates the billable resources, restores the last backup, and runs doctor. Nearly all of it is Cloud SQL provisioning; the Memgraph VM serves Bolt after roughly two minutes, so the graph is usable well before the database is. Start a session before you need it.

nodes.rationale: Five tasks: db.py, graph_client.py, setup_memgraph.py, Makefile/docs, and live verification. Written after establishing that db.py is a rewrite rather than a port.

nodes.label: Scope Split by Consumer
nodes.rationale: memgraph_client.py is 1181 lines across 37 functions. Porting all of it would add ~20 functions with no caller until Phase 8 and no way to test them beyond asserting a query string contains MERGE -- coverage theatre. Split by who calls it instead: driver and write path now, ~16 read functions to Phase 8, quality inputs to Phase 7, three provenance writers to v2 per ADR-008, migrate_schema_v5 dropped.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — Connectors (DONE)
nodes.rationale: Completed 2026-08-20. All four exit criteria met against the real Onix account: 50 emails and 100 calendar events staged, re-running staged zero, a corrupted token produced a visible INGESTION IS STOPPED alert, and all 317 tests are mocked with no live credentials.

nodes.label: Phase 5 Connectors Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: Eight tasks: watermarks and the Source protocol, google_auth, Gmail, Calendar, Jira, Meet, jobs/ entrypoints, and live verification. One shared token helper and one shared watermark store rather than four connectors each with a subtly different implementation.

nodes.label: Calendar 410 Gone — Permanent Breakage After First Success
nodes.norm_label: calendar 410 gone — permanent breakage after first success
nodes.rationale: updatedMin outside Calendar's incremental window is rejected with 410 Gone. Without a fallback the connector breaks permanently after its FIRST successful run -- ingestion stops at exactly the point it starts working. Fixed with a fallback to a full sync, per Google's documented remedy. The 410 proved intermittent: an immediate re-run got a 200 for the same updatedMin, which makes the fallback more valuable, not less, since the failure appears at random. Found only by running the connector twice, invisible to review and to the mocked suite.

nodes.label: mypy Caught a Source-Type Mismatch Before It Ran
nodes.norm_label: mypy caught a source-type mismatch before it ran
nodes.rationale: The connectors had invented calendar_event, jira_issue and meet_transcript, none of which are in models.SourceType (email | calendar | meet | jira). Phase 6's pipeline would not have recognised a single staged row, and nothing would have failed loudly -- the rows would simply sit unprocessed forever. Caught by mypy before any test ran, then locked down by a dedicated test.

nodes.label: No Path From Auth Spike to Connectors
nodes.norm_label: no path from auth spike to connectors
nodes.rationale: google_auth read only GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN from settings, but Phase 0.5's auth spike writes the token to token.json. Settings still win, since that is what Cloud Run injects from Secret Manager; token.json is now the local-development fallback.

nodes.label: TranscriptSource Shares a Name, Not a Concept
nodes.norm_label: transcriptsource shares a name, not a concept
nodes.rationale: v5's TranscriptSource is a read-already-staged-rows seam, because Airbyte did the fetching. v6's Source protocol fetches from upstream and stages. Only jira_client.py and meet.py were genuine ports; Gmail, Calendar and the Jira source are new code, since Airbyte handled those in v5.

nodes.label: Verified Against Local Postgres, Not Cloud SQL
nodes.norm_label: verified against local postgres, not cloud sql
nodes.rationale: The connectors need the real Google APIs, not Cloud SQL specifically. ADR-015 guarantees identical queries run unmodified against both, and Phase 3 already proved the Cloud SQL path, so this avoided a roughly 12-minute billable sync-up for no additional evidence.

nodes.label: Disabled Sources Are No-Ops, Not Errors
nodes.norm_label: disabled sources are no-ops, not errors
nodes.rationale: Jira without credentials and Meet without a Pub/Sub subscription both return cleanly with zero records rather than raising, because tiers 0 and 1 must run the whole pipeline with neither configured.

nodes.label: Watermark Advances Only After Staging Succeeds
nodes.norm_label: watermark advances only after staging succeeds
nodes.rationale: Advancing the watermark before staging succeeds means a mid-batch failure skips those records permanently, and nothing surfaces the loss until someone notices a week of meetings is missing. stage_all() stages every fetched record first and only then advances the watermark, using the maximum watermark seen rather than the last, since sources do not always return records in order.
